facts.statement: Proaethaspis is an extinct genus containing only one species of arthrodire placoderm fish that lived during the Early Devonian period.
facts.quote: Proaethaspis is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm fish from the Early Devonian period.

facts.statement: The type species Proaethaspis ohioensis was first described in 1960 and later assigned to the genus Proaethaspis in 1978.
facts.quote: The type species Proaethaspis ohioensis was described in 1960, but was assigned to the genus Proaethaspis in 1978.

facts.statement: Proaethaspis is considered one of the most basal members of the order Arthrodira and is closely related to the genus Baringaspis.
facts.quote: Proaethaspis is one of the more basal members of the order Arthrodira, closely related to Baringaspis

facts.statement: Proaethaspis belongs to the family Actinolepididae.
Fossils of Proaethaspis date from the Lochkovian to the Pragian stages, between 419.62 and 410.62 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lochkovian to Pragian (419.62 to 410.62 million years ago)
